newsitem.title: TURKEY: Cegelec wins Istanbul subway tender.
newsitem.headline: Cegelec wins Istanbul subway tender.

text.p: A consortium led by France's Cegelec won a tender held by the Istanbul city council for electro-mechanical works on a newly constructed 7.8-km subway line, a city spokeswoman said on Thursday.
She said the tender was awarded for $180 million to Cegelec consortium after two weeks of negotiations. The consortium includes Turkish Cengiz Construction and Albayrak A.S.

"The tender was finalised today. A contract will be signed with Cegelec consortium within 10 days. All of the project will be financed by foreign credits and the work will be completed in 18 months," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
Cegelec gradually reduced its bid from an original price of $208.9 million.

The tender covered power supply, track laying, traction, signalling, telecommunication, storage facilites and station fitting, but excludes supply of train carriages. The 7.8 km line links Istanbul's 4.Levent and Taksim districts.
The city had received three bids for the tender which closed on November 7, 1996. Other bidding consortia were led by Canadian Bombardier Inc and ABB Traction AB.
Officials said two weeks ago that Bombardier had maintained its bid at $282.75 million at the start of negotiations while ABB Traction had dropped out of the tender.

Istanbul's municipality cancelled in October 1996 a first tender for the electro-mechanisation of the subway line which was awarded for $224 million in October 1995 to a consortium led by Turk Siemens, largely owned by German Siemens AG.

The tender was cancelled because a detailed technical contract was not signed in time although an extension was granted by the municipality. But Turk Siemens officials have denied this and blamed the city for demanding new terms which caused the technical contract to be delayed.
